# 1 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_002_page_001.jpg

---

1. In those days Mattathias son of John, son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, arose from Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
2. And he had five sons: John, called Gaddi;
3. Simon, called Thassi;
4. Judas, called Maccabeus;
5. Eleazar, called Avaran; and Jonathan, called Apphus.
6. And he saw the blasphemies that were being done in Judah and in Jerusalem,
7. and he said, "Woe to me! Why was I born to see this — the ruin of my people and the ruin of the holy city — and to dwell there when she was given into the hand of enemies, and the sanctuary into the hand of strangers?
8. Her temple has become like a man without honor.
9. The vessels of her glory have been carried away into exile; her infants have been slain in her streets, her young men by the sword of the enemy.
10. What nation has not inherited her palace and not seized her spoils?
11. All her adornment has been taken away; instead of a free woman she has become a slave.
12. And behold, our holy things, our beauty, and our glory have been laid waste, and the nations have defiled them.
13. Why then should we live any longer?"
14. And Mattathias and his sons tore their garments and put on sackcloth and mourned exceedingly.
15. And the king's officers who were enforcing the apostasy came to the city of Modein to make them sacrifice.
16. And many from Israel came to them, and Mattathias and his sons came together.
17. Then the king's officers answered and said to Mattathias: "You are a leader and a distinguished and great man in this city, and strengthened with sons and brothers.
18. Now come first and do the command of the king, as all the nations have done and the men of Judah and those who have remained in Jerusalem; and you and your house will be among the friends of the king, and you and your sons will be honored with silver and gold and many gifts."
19. And Mattathias answered and said in a loud voice: "Even if all the nations that are in the house of the king's dominion obey him and fall away, each from the worship of his fathers, and choose to follow his commands,
20. yet I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
21. God forbid that we should forsake the Torah and the ordinances.
22. We will not listen to the words of the king, to turn aside from our worship, to the right hand or to the left."
23. And when he had finished speaking these words, a certain Jew came forward in the sight of all to sacrifice upon the altar in Modein according to the king's command.
24. And Mattathias saw and was jealous with zeal, and his kidneys trembled, and he was moved according to the law; and he ran and slew him upon the altar.
25. And the king's officer who was compelling them to sacrifice he slew at that time also, and he tore down the altar.
26. And he was zealous for the Torah just as Phinehas did to Zimri son of Salu.
27. And Mattathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying, "Let everyone who is zealous for the Torah and who maintains the covenant follow me!"
28. And he and his sons fled to the hills and left behind all that they had in the city.
29. Then many who were seeking justice and judgment went down to the wilderness to dwell there —
30. they and their sons and their wives and their cattle — because evils had increased upon them.
31. And it was reported to the king's officers and to the forces that were in Jerusalem, the city of David, that men who had disregarded the king's command had gone down to the hiding places in the wilderness.
32. And many ran after them and overtook them; and they encamped against them and drew up battle against them on the sabbath day.
33. And they said to them, "Now come out and do as the king commands, and you will live."
34. And they said, "We will not come out, and we will not do the word of the king, to profane the sabbath day."
35. And they hastened to attack them.
36. But they did not answer them, nor did they cast a stone at them, nor block the hiding places,
37. saying, "Let us all die in our innocence; heaven and earth are witnesses over us that you destroy us unjustly."
38. And they attacked them on the sabbath, and they died — they and their wives and their children and their cattle — about a thousand souls.
39. And Mattathias and his friends heard and mourned greatly for them.
40. And one man said to his neighbor, "If we all do as our brothers have done and do not fight against the nations for our lives and our ordinances, they will quickly destroy us from the earth."
41. And they took counsel on that day, saying, "Every man, whoever attacks us on the sabbath day — let us fight against him, and we will not all die as our brothers died in the hiding places."
42. Then there gathered to them a congregation of the Hasideans, mighty men of Israel, everyone who offered himself willingly for the Torah.
43. And all who were fleeing from the evils joined them and became a support to them.
44. And they organized an army and struck sinners in their anger, and lawless men in their wrath; and the survivors fled to the nations.
45. And Mattathias and his friends went around and tore down the altars.
46. And they forcibly circumcised all the uncircumcised children whom they found in the borders of Israel.
47. And they drove away the arrogant, and the work prospered in their hands.
48. And they rescued the Torah out of the hand of the nations and out of the hand of the kings, and they did not give the advantage to the sinner.
49. And the days of Mattathias drew near to die, and he said to his sons, "Now arrogance and reproach have grown mighty, and a time of destruction and hot wrath has come.
50. Now, children, be zealous for the Torah and give your lives for the covenant of our fathers.
51. And remember the deeds that our fathers did in their generations, and receive great honor and an everlasting name.
52. Was not Abraham found faithful in trial, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness?
53. Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and he became lord of Egypt.
54. Phinehas our father, because he was exceedingly zealous with zeal, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
55. Joshua, because he fulfilled the word, became a judge in Israel.
56. Caleb, because he bore witness in the congregation, received the inheritance in the land.
57. David, because he was merciful, inherited the throne of a kingdom forever and ever.
58. Elijah, because he was exceedingly zealous for the Torah, was taken up into heaven.
59. Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael believed and were saved from the flame.
60. Daniel, in his innocence, was delivered from the mouth of the lions.
61. And so consider this, generation by generation, that none who trust in him will lack strength.
62. And do not be afraid of the words of a sinful man, for his glory will be dung and worms.
63. Today he is exalted, and tomorrow he cannot be found, for he has returned to his dust, and his purpose has perished.
64. And you, children, be strong and courageous in the Torah, for in it you will be glorified.
65. And behold, Simon your brother — I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him all your days; he shall be a father to you.
66. And Judas Maccabeus — he has been mighty in strength from his youth; he shall be your commander and wage the war of the people.
67. And you shall receive to yourselves all who observe the Torah, and execute the vengeance of your people.
68. Render recompense to the nations, and give heed to the commandment of the Torah.
69. And he blessed them and was added to his fathers.
70. And he died in the one hundred and forty-sixth year, and his sons buried him in the tombs of his fathers in Modein, and all Israel made great lamentation over him.
